newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to re-offer 10 pct Electro Cables.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to re-offer 10 pct Electro Cables.

text.p: An Egyptian state-owned firm has decided to re-offer investors a stake in partly privatised Egyptian Electro Cables after price fluctuations dampened the first offer, the agents for the sale said on Monday.
The state offered investors at least 10 percent or 330,000 shares in Egyptian Electro Cables at a minimum price of 124 pounds ($36.5) for two days on May 13.

Nadir Ezzedin at the investment department of the National Bank of Egypt told Reuters investors did not subscribe to the offering because the minimum offering price was higher than the stock's trading price on the bourse.
"We've cancelled that offering and we're going to do it again in a different way," Ezzedin said.
The state-owned Engineering Industries Company owns a majority 70 percent of Egyptian Electro Cables while private investors hold 21.7 percent. The employees hold the remaining 8.3 percent.
Egyptian Electro Cables has a total 3.3 million shares since it split its shares 10 for one in October 1996.
